'''Aissa Wade'''  is a professor of [[Mathematics]] at the [[Pennsylvania State University]]. She was the President of the [[African Institute for Mathematical Sciences]] centre in Senegal (from 2016 to 2018).

== Early life and education ==
Wade was born in [[Dakar]], [[Senegal]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.icm2022-paris.com/medias/content/files/Aissa_Wade.pdf|title=Aissa Wade|website=ICM 2022|access-date=2018-05-25|archive-date=2018-05-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180526041431/https://www.icm2022-paris.com/medias/content/files/Aissa_Wade.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> She studied mathematics at [[Cheikh Anta Diop University]] and graduated in 1993.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/wade_aissa.html|title=Aissa Wade, Mathematician of the African Diaspora|website=www.math.buffalo.edu|access-date=2018-05-25}}</ref> She had to leave [[Senegal]] to earn a Ph.D. as there were no opportunities in Africa.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dw.com/en/transforming-africa-with-science-and-technology/a-19060805|title=Transforming Africa with science and technology? {{!}} DW {{!}} 25.02.2016|last=(www.dw.com)|first=Deutsche Welle|website=DW.COM|language=en|access-date=2018-05-25}}</ref> Wade earned her Ph.D. at the [[University of Montpellier]] in 1996.<ref name=":0" /> Her thesis, ''"Normalisation formelle de structures de Poisson"'', considered [[symplectic geometry]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=African doctorates in mathematics : a catalogue|last=Paulus|first=Gerdes|author-link=Paulus Gerdes|date=2007|publisher=Research Centre for Mathematics, Culture and Education|others=African Mathematical Union. Commission on the History of Mathematics in Africa.|isbn=9781430318675|location=Maputo, Mozambique|oclc=123226819}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1997-03-01|title=Normalisation formelle de structures de Poisson|journal=Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I|language=en|volume=324|issue=5|pages=531–536|doi=10.1016/S0764-4442(99)80385-1|issn=0764-4442|bibcode=1997CRASM.324..531W|last1=Wade|first1=Aïssa}}</ref> Her doctoral advisor was Jean Paul Dufour.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=31158|title=Aïssa Wade - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.ams.org|access-date=2018-05-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dufour|first1=Jean-Paul|last2=Wade|first2=Aissa|date=2008|title=On the local structure of Dirac manifolds|arxiv=math/0405257|journal=Compositio Mathematica|volume=144|issue=3|pages=774–786|doi=10.1112/S0010437X07003272|s2cid=119153423 |issn=0010-437X}}</ref>

== Career ==
Wade became a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics]], where she worked on conformal Dirac structures.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.iaea.org/inis/collection/NCLCollectionStore/_Public/31/051/31051269.pdf|title=Conformal Dirac Structures|last=Wade|first=Aissa|website=IAEA|access-date=2018-05-25}}</ref> She held visiting faculty positions at [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], [[African University of Science and Technology]] and [[Paul Sabatier University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.yase-conference.eu/index.php/en/11-pages-en/145-aissa-wade-en|title=Aissa Wade - EN|last=Allemand|first=Luc|website=YASE Conference|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-05-25|archive-date=2018-07-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180709121757/http://www.yase-conference.eu/index.php/en/11-pages-en/145-aissa-wade-en|url-status=dead}}</ref> Wade joined [[Pennsylvania State University]] and was appointed full professor in 2016.

She served as a managing editor of The African Diaspora Journal of Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-15 |title={{!}} Mathematical Research Publishers |url=https://math-res-pub.org/adjm/editorial-board |access-date=2024-01-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210415110702/https://math-res-pub.org/adjm/editorial-board |archive-date=2021-04-15 }}</ref> She is editor of Afrika Mathematika.<ref name=":1" /> She is on the scientific committee of the [[NextEinstein]] forum, an initiative to connect science, society and policy in Africa.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://nef.org/about-us/spc/aissa-wade/|title=Aissa Wade|date=2015-12-02|work=Next Einstein Forum|access-date=2018-05-25|language=en-US|archive-date=2018-07-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180708191621/https://nef.org/about-us/spc/aissa-wade/|url-status=dead}}</ref> As the President of the [[African Institute for Mathematical Sciences]], Wade was the first woman to hold this role.<ref>{{Citation|last=groupe|first=G. I. D.|title=1er Forum GID-FastDev - Mme Aissa Wade|date=2016-03-16|url=https://vimeo.com/159193045|accessdate=2018-05-25}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://aasciences.ac.ke/aas/en/recognising-excellence/aas-fellows-in-senegal-/|title=AAS Fellows in Senegal|website=African Academy of Sciences|language=en|access-date=2018-05-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180526041255/https://aasciences.ac.ke/aas/en/recognising-excellence/aas-fellows-in-senegal-/|archive-date=2018-05-26|url-status=dead}}</ref> She has been awarded funding from the [[National Science Foundation]] to support the Senegal Workshop on Geometric Structures.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1208297|title=NSF Award Search: Award#1208297 - Senegal Workshop on Geometric Structures and Control Theory|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2018-05-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0715543|title=NSF Award Search: Award#0715543 - International Conference on Geometry and Physics|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2018-05-25}}</ref> She has been involved with [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] activities to enhance African [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]] research, including the provision of evidence-based metrics, case studies and policy recommendations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wpi.edu/sites/default/files/docs/Offices/Dean-of-Engineering/Aissa%20Wade-%20Global%20Best%20Practices-ilovepdf-compressed.pdf|title=Global Best Practices Creating a pipeline for STEM @ AIMS|date=2017-05-15|website=Worcester Polytechnic Institute|access-date=2018-05-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://aaas.confex.com/aaas/2016/webprogram/Session12012.html|title=Session: Enhancing African STEM Research and Capacity with International Collaboration (2016 AAAS Annual Meeting (February 11-15, 2016))|website=aaas.confex.com|access-date=2018-05-25}}</ref> In 2017 Wade was named a fellow of the [[African Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.universityworldnews.com/article.php?story=2018030909095990|title=University dons dominate new list of AAS fellows - University World News|website=www.universityworldnews.com|access-date=2018-05-25}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

Wade's accomplishments earned her recognition by ''[[Mathematically Gifted & Black]],'' where she was featured as a Black History Month 2020 Honoree.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Aissa Wade|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/aissa-wade/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black}}</ref>
